subject: music
title: Tempo Changes
welcome_lead: Speeding up, slowing down, holding back.
meta_desc: KS3 tempo: accelerando, ritardando, rubato, tempo changes.
final_note: Composers use changes in speed for drama.

walkthroughs.body_html: Accelerando (accel.) means gradually get faster. Used to build excitement — chase scenes, races, climaxes.
Ritardando (rit.) means gradually slow down. Often used at the end of a piece or before a return to the main theme.
Rubato means 'stolen time' — the player stretches some notes and rushes others for expression. A fermata (bird's-eye) over a note means hold it longer.
